Chris Coons

Democratic candidate for U.S. Senator, Delaware · Incumbent

U.S. Senator from Delaware

Chris Coons is a Democrat who has represented Delaware in the U.S. Senate since winning a 2010 election, and he is running for another term. He won the Democratic primary on Sept. 15, 2026, beating Jeff Appelhans, Eric No-Trump Hansen and Mary Louve. In the Nov. 3 general election he faces Republican Dr. Michael "Mike" Katz.

Where Coons stands

Campaign priorities
Says his priorities are opportunity, security and justice: raising wages, protecting residents from threats abroad and at home, and rooting out corruption in Washington.
Federal spending and debt
Says both parties share responsibility for deficits. Supports raising taxes on wealthy Americans and highly profitable corporations while giving relief to working families.
Social Security
Supports raising the income cap on Social Security payroll taxes. Supports a bipartisan process to consider other changes to strengthen the program.
Health care
Defends the Affordable Care Act as a way to expand access to insurance and preventive care. Argues that better access to primary care can reduce costly emergency treatment.
Tariffs and trade
Opposes the Trump administration's broad tariffs, arguing they raise prices for consumers and businesses, including Delaware's chemical, agriculture and port industries. Favors removing trade barriers.
Iran
Opposes the administration's conduct of the war with Iran, citing poor planning and too little consultation with Congress and allies. Calls for ending the conflict and reopening shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Ukraine
Supports continued U.S. support for Ukraine against Russia's invasion.
Senate filibuster
Supports keeping the Senate filibuster. Is open to some reforms, especially for voting rights legislation.
Immigration
Supports border security combined with more accountability for federal immigration enforcement and legal pathways for qualifying immigrants.
Artificial intelligence
Supports responsible AI development, with an emphasis on safeguards and on how data centers affect local communities.
